target.title: fix(android): stop killing long chat runs with hardcoded timeouts (#106863)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Any agent turn longer than ~2 minutes started from the Android app ends in an error, while the identical turn over Telegram completes fine. Full analysis in #106863. Two independent causes, both in `ChatController.kt`:

1. `buildChatSendParams` hardcodes `timeoutMs: 30_000` into every `chat.send`. The gateway uses that as the server-side run expiry (`resolveAgentTimeoutMs({ cfg, overrideMs: p.timeoutMs })` in `chat-send-session.ts`), so the maintenance sweep aborts app-initiated runs that outlive ~30 s + grace ("CLI run aborted" / "Embedded agent failed before reply"). Other channels get the config default (48 h). Queued sends burn their expiry budget before their turn even starts.
2. `armPendingRunTimeout` fires after a hard 120 s, refreshes the history snapshot, computes `runStillInFlight` — and then declares a timeout **even when the run is confirmed in flight**: spurious "Timed out waiting for a reply" banner, optimistic bubble removed, outbox row parked as Failed/delivery-unconfirmed. Streaming deltas never re-arm the timer, so this hits actively streaming turns too.

## Fix

- Omit `timeoutMs` from `chat.send` so app runs get the gateway's configured default expiry, same as other channels.
- In `armPendingRunTimeout`, when the post-delay snapshot confirms the run is still in flight, re-arm the timer and keep waiting instead of timing out. The not-in-flight path is unchanged; terminal events and the server-side expiry remain the liveness backstop, so a genuinely dead run still resolves (and `wasTimedOut` recovery is untouched).

## Evidence

- Verified the equivalent server-side behavior on a live gateway (Android/Termux host where turns of 2–11+ min are routine): with the 30 s override neutralized, app-initiated long turns complete exactly like Telegram ones instead of ~50% dying to run expiry.
- The client-timer change follows the existing state machine (`clearPendingRun`/`timedOutRunIds` paths unchanged); I couldn't run a Gradle build on this ARM64/PRoot device, so a CI build/emulator pass would be appreciated.

Fixes #106863

target.title: fix(nostr): keep profile imports as cancellable drafts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Nostr profile imports could mutate config before the user reviewed relay data. While an import was pending, a same-field edit could be overwritten by the response. Cancel could close the form while a server-side merge still persisted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI now requests `autoMerge: false`, treats relay data as a draft, locks profile controls while importing, and aborts/invalidate imports on Cancel, disconnect, or form replacement. Late responses cannot update a hidden or newer form. Explicit **Save & Publish** remains the write path.

The existing HTTP contract is preserved: callers that explicitly send `autoMerge: true` retain server-side merge and persistence. Only the Control UI opts into draft mode.

## User Impact

Imported values fill the open form for review. Users can edit and explicitly publish them; Cancel cannot hide a persisted mutation, and stale responses cannot replace a newer form.

## Evidence

### Real Control UI + relay/browser proof

A standalone Chromium run drove the actual Control UI. Its import request was forwarded to the actual `createNostrProfileHttpHandler`, which queried the public relay `wss://nos.lol`. The server held the response until after the browser clicked Cancel; completion then produced no config write. The browser reopened the form and verified the local value remained, then exercised **Save & Publish** and observed the expected PUT and success UI.

Redacted output:

```json
{
  "browser": "Chromium",
  "relay": "wss://nos.lol",
  "pubkeyPrefix": "c938f0bd…",
  "relayPublish": "accepted",
  "pendingImport": { "browserRequest": { "autoMerge": false }, "fieldsDisabled": true },
  "cancel": {
    "clientAction": "Cancel",
    "serverCompletedAfterCancel": true,
    "serverPersistenceCalls": 0,
    "persistedProfile": { "name": "local" },
    "formValueAfterReopen": "local",
    "requestWasDelayedUntilCancel": true
  },
  "saveAndPublish": {
    "requestMethod": "PUT",
    "requestBody": { "name": "saved-draft" },
    "uiSuccess": true
  }
}
```

The run generated pending-import, after-Cancel/reopen, and after-Save screenshots plus a Chromium WebM recording under `.artifacts/control-ui-e2e/nostr-live-proof/`. The browser run was against the same implementation before the final rebases; those rebases only added current-main commits outside this PR’s changed paths.

### CI/base diagnosis and focused validation

- The earlier Apple i18n failure (`checks-node-compact-small-2`, run `29220125349`) was on old base `f26793ca54`; the PR never touched `apps/ios/Sources/Design/SettingsProTabSections.swift`. Current main contains the wrapper fix, and the later exact-head run passed that shard.
- Exact-head run `29220974456` identified the branch-specific guard failure: `ui/src/pages/channels/channels-page.ts` grew from 514 to 538 lines. This follow-up splits page-local Nostr helpers into `nostr-profile-operation.ts`, leaves the page at 497 lines, and removes its obsolete LOC baseline entry.
- The same exact-head run’s dependency failure listed only existing `src/agents/*` and `src/gateway/*` unused-export ratchet entries; no changed PR path was listed. Current-main CI independently reported the same dependency/guard job failures.
- Final sync base: `156f4c89ed0325049c6d83968d5a76c59ee7ff6d`.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/nostr/src/nostr-profile-http.test.ts extensions/nostr/src/nostr-profile-import.test.ts` — 34 tests passed.

- Scoped `oxfmt` and `oxlint` passed for the changed UI and Nostr files.

## Limitations

The browser Save & Publish evidence uses the UI’s PUT request with a deterministic successful response; it does not claim a live publish from a running Nostr bus. target.title: fix(whatsapp): add chunk-idle timeout to inbound media download
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where WhatsApp inbound media downloads that stall after Baileys returns a stream (headers/start ok, then no further chunks) would block `downloadInboundMedia` forever via `saveMediaStream`'s unbounded `for await`, so inbound dispatch never produces an agent reply for that message.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Wrap the Baileys AsyncIterable with a local per-chunk idle race (production default `30_000` ms), matching Telegram's download idle floor and the LINE channel pattern (open `#86873`, different owner).
- On timeout, reject with `WhatsAppInboundMediaTimeoutError`, call `iterator.return()` so Node Readable streams are destroyed, and silence the losing `next()` to avoid `unhandledRejection`.
- Tests may pass a short `chunkTimeoutMs`; production omits it and uses the 30s floor (proven with fake timers).
- Does **not** change core `saveMediaStream` / `src/media/store.ts` (avoids competing with LINE `#86873`).
- Timeout error class stays module-private (knip unused-export gate).

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled WhatsApp media body could hang inbound handling for that message indefinitely.

**After:** Idle streams fail closed after 30s with a clear timeout error so the monitor loop can continue.

## Evidence

Head: `2de7b8c91e1ed785a490369117ad51915e6ea6d2`

### Executable negative control + wrap proof

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/media.node.test.ts -- --run -t "chunk-idle|negative" --reporter=verbose
```

```text

[whatsapp media idle proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=53 chunkTimeoutMs=50 production_ms=30000

```

## Real behavior proof

Production `downloadInboundMedia` → real `saveMediaStream` (no media-store mock) with a stalled Baileys AsyncIterable.


target.title: fix(dreaming): drop heartbeat assistant responses from dream corpus
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The dreaming ingestion pipeline filters heartbeat **user** messages (containing `[OpenClaw heartbeat poll]`) via `sanitizeSessionText`, but the paired **assistant** response was only dropped when it was the exact string `HEARTBEAT_OK`. Local models frequently respond with natural-language acknowledgments (e.g. "Heartbeat received. Main is active.") which pass through the sanitizer unchanged and enter the dream corpus as low-confidence memory snippets.

See issue #103720.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original text-based heartbeat detection was user-spoofable (anyone could type the heartbeat marker and trigger the drop). The fix uses **runtime provenance** (`provenance: { kind: "heartbeat" }`) attached at the source in `get-reply-run.ts`, which cannot be spoofed by user input.

For existing workspaces with heartbeat contamination, the `doctor` audit/repair system:
- Scans session-corpus files for heartbeat-derived lines via source refs
- Removes only heartbeat lines while preserving normal content
- Handles **both file-backed sessions** (`.jsonl` paths) and **SQLite-backed sessions** (logical paths without extension) via a fallback to `loadTranscriptEventsSync`
- Avoids clearing session ingestion checkpoints to prevent corpus duplication on re-ingestion
- Falls through to self-ingestion narrative content checks even when heartbeat contamination is found

## User Impact

- **No visible change** for users without heartbeat contamination
- **Lower memory noise** for users with heartbeat-enabled sessions — average 0.58-confidence heartbeat-derived entries are removed from dream corpus
- **One-time cleanup** via `openclaw doctor` for existing workspaces
- **No data loss** — heartbeat lines are archived before removal, normal corpus lines are preserved

## Evidence

### Forward Prevention (Provenance-based)
- Heartbeat turns carry `provenance: { kind: "heartbeat" }` attached at the source in `get-reply-run.ts`
- `buildSessionEntry` checks `message.provenance.kind === "heartbeat"` instead of text-matching user content
- When a heartbeat user message is filtered, the immediately following assistant response is also dropped via a `pendingHeartbeatUserDrop` flag
- Cross-message coupling is gated by runtime provenance (not user-spoofable text per PR #70737)

### Backward Repair (Targeted Doctor Audit)
- `auditDreamingArtifacts` + `repairDreamingArtifacts` functions available via `openclaw doctor`
- Detects and archives heartbeat-derived session-corpus entries, contaminated session-ingestion state, and duplicate diary entries
- Handles both file-backed and SQLite logical session paths in corpus references

### Validation
- [x] Format: `oxfmt --check` passes
- [x] Lint: `oxlint --deny curly` passes
- [x] Extension tests: 63 files, 1046/1046 tests pass
- [x] Type check: `tsgo` passes
- [x] Autoreview: 2 P1s fixed (checkpoint clearing, path resolution), 2 remaining known issues in pre-existing code

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.ts` | `pendingHeartbeatUserDrop` flag + provenance-based heartbeat detection |
| `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts` | Tests: heartbeat provenance filtering |
| `src/sessions/input-provenance.ts` | Export heartbeat provenance kind constant |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.ts` | Attach `provenance: { kind: "heartbeat" }` to heartbeat replies |
| `extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-repair.ts` | New: audit + repair functions for dreaming artifacts |
| `extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-repair.test.ts` | Tests for dreaming repair |
| `src/commands/doctor-memory-search.ts` | Integrate dreaming audit/repair into doctor command |
| `src/commands/doctor-memory-search.test.ts` | Update mocks for new imports |
| `src/plugin-sdk/sqlite-runtime-testing.ts` | Export `loadTranscriptEventsSync` for repair fallback |
| `src/plugin-sdk/memory-core-engine-runtime.ts` | Export `repairDreamingArtifacts` |
| `src/plugin-sdk/memory-core-bundled-runtime.ts` | Export `repairDreamingArtifacts` |

target.title: fix(exec): memoize duplicate auto-review verdicts
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the exec approval path and understand the authorization boundary changed by this patch.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102249.

The model-backed exec auto-reviewer pays for a fresh reviewer completion whenever the same ask-requiring request is reviewed again. Retry and polling loops can therefore turn N identical reviews into N paid model calls even though the reviewer runs deterministically at temperature 0.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a bounded per-reviewer-instance memo with conservative, host-bound reuse semantics:

- cache only completed low-risk `allow-once` decisions;
- key the memo on the full reviewer input, including gateway `resolvedPath`;
- bind node-host reuse to both canonical `nodeId` and the executable identity pinned by `system.run.prepare`;
- force a fresh review when command, argv, executable identity, node target, cwd, environment keys, host, reason, analysis, or agent context changes;
- never cache `ask`, timeout, unavailable-model, completion-error, or other conservative fallback outcomes;
- cap the memo at 128 entries.

The approval host still consumes each returned `allow-once` decision once and rechecks current policy before dispatch. This patch does not persist decisions or change reviewer prompts, model routing, auth, or approval policy. Reuse of tightly bound low-risk verdicts remains an explicit maintainer policy decision.

## User Impact

For N byte-identical requests within one reviewer instance, paid reviewer completions drop from N to 1. A different node target or prepared executable always triggers a fresh completion, preventing one host's verdict from crossing an execution boundary.

## Evidence

Final rebase:

- `upstream/main`: `055f6649f97`
- branch head: `574003cc734`

Validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts` -> 85/85 tests passed on the final rebased head.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main --timed` -> all selected gates passed before the final baseline-only rebase, including core typecheck (42.64s), core-test typecheck (822.82s), changed-file lint (110.30s), LOC, format, dependency pin, import-cycle, database-first, and security guards.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` -> passed on the final rebased head.

Configured provider-backed runtime proof used OpenClaw's production config validation, reviewer model/auth resolution, `completeSimple`, and OpenAI-compatible streaming HTTP transport against a local deterministic endpoint. It was not an installed Gateway/paired-node E2E and incurred no external model usage.

| Request | Cumulative real completion POSTs |
| --- | ---: |
| baseline | 1 |
| byte-identical repeat | 1 |
| changed `nodeId` | 2 |
| changed executable identity | 3 |

All three completion calls were `POST /v1/chat/completions` with the configured bearer auth, `model=reviewer-proof`, `stream=true`, and `temperature=0`. Each returned a parsed low-risk `allow-once` decision. The captured prompts contained the expected node and executable bindings.

Focused invariants:

- duplicate low-risk input: model completion count `2 -> 1`;
- changed argv, gateway resolved path, node target, or node executable identity: fresh completion;
- duplicate `ask`: two completions, no memo reuse;
- node host forwards the prepared executable identity and canonical target node.

Signed-off-by: Ho Lim <subhoya@gmail.com>

target.title: fix(zalo): bound proxy fetcher cache to 64 entries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Zalo `resolveZaloProxyFetch` retained one `makeProxyFetch` entry per distinct proxy URL in a process-lifetime `Map` with no eviction. Config churn or high-cardinality proxy URLs could therefore grow gateway memory without a hard bound.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Cap `proxyCache` at 64 entries using the shared `pruneMapToMaxSize` helper after every successful insert (same pattern as Nextcloud Talk room cache / MS Teams team-group cache / Mattermost opaque-target cache).
- Insertion-order eviction keeps newest proxy fetchers; cache-hit identity and empty-URL behavior are unchanged.
- Adds a focused regression that fills `max+1` distinct URLs, proves the oldest entry is rebuilt on next use, and confirms a mid-window entry still hits.

No new config/env surface. Does not change Bot API timeouts (`#104017`) or other Zalo send paths.

## User Impact

**Before:** Long-running Zalo gateways could retain an unbounded number of proxy fetcher closures as distinct proxy URLs appeared.

**After:** At most 64 distinct proxy fetchers are retained; older ones are dropped and rebuilt on next use.

## Evidence

Head: `4d348f869a9b7395123a205cc2545e1f1a3c0ea2`

### Unit + executable negative control

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/zalo/src/proxy.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```text
[zalo proxyCache negative control] unbounded_size=65 unbounded_keeps_oldest=true bounded_size=64 bounded_evicts_oldest=true
[zalo proxyCache proof] max=64 filled=65 oldest_evicted=true rebuilt=true mid_hit=true
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

### Real behavior proof (production path)

No `makeProxyFetch` mock. Calls production `resolveZaloProxyFetch` → SDK `makeProxyFetch` (Undici `ProxyAgent` wrappers) against 65 distinct loopback proxy URLs.

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/zalo/src/proxy.proof.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```text
[zalo proxyCache production proof] max=64 filled=65 oldest_evicted=true rebuilt=true mid_hit=true real_makeProxyFetch=true
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

- **Boundary crossed:** process-local Undici ProxyAgent-backed fetch wrappers (real `makeProxyFetch`), no fetch-runtime mock.
- **Negative control:** plain Map without `pruneMapToMaxSize` retains oldest after 65 inserts; production path rebuilds oldest after the 64-entry cap.
- **Siblings:** Nextcloud Talk / MS Teams / Mattermost `pruneMapToMaxSize` callers unchanged.
- **CI note:** `checks-node-compact-small-1` fail on `test/scripts/test-extension.test.ts` (`readdirSync: 54`) is tooling flake unrelated to this Zalo surface.

target.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits at 30s
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using Codex app-server over `websocket`/`unix` transport would hang forever on `initialize`/RPC when a peer accepted TCP but never completed the WebSocket upgrade. Pending frames never flush and the client never sees a transport exit, so the run cannot fail closed or reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add a private `buildCodexAppServerWebSocketOptions` that sets `handshakeTimeout: 30_000` (same floor as Slack relay / Mattermost / Discord gateway).
- Both TCP and Unix upgrade paths consume that builder.
- Guard `EventEmitter` error re-emit with `listenerCount` so callers that only wait on `exit` (handshake hang paths) are not disrupted by Node's unhandled-`error` throw.
- Regressions observe production wiring in source (knip-safe) and prove stalled-handshake exit + `initialize` failure with a short test-only hang floor.

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A Codex app-server endpoint that accepted TCP without completing the websocket handshake could pin `initialize`/RPC forever on that attempt.

**After:** Handshake waits fail closed after 30s (`Opening handshake has timed out` → transport `exit` / client error), so the run can stop or recover instead of hanging.

## Evidence

Head: `a02be68e1107857c4808cc9e93e1af5b10c7f1f1`

### Wiring + hang regression

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```text
[codex handshake negative control] outcome=still-pending readyState=0 wait_ms=300 without_handshakeTimeout=true
[codex handshake proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=200 code=1006 handshakeTimeout_ms=200 production_ms=30000
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** TCP-accept / never-upgrade pins Codex app-server `initialize`/RPC with no transport exit.
- **Canonical path:** production `createWebSocketTransport` → private builder with `handshakeTimeout: CODEX_APP_SERVER_WS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS` (30s).
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime TCP; real `ws` against loopback `net.Server` that accepts but never upgrades (no handshake mock).
- **Negative control:** plain `ws.WebSocket` **without** `handshakeTimeout` stays `CONNECTING` / `still-pending` after 300ms on the same fixture.
- **After fix:** short test floor exits ~200ms with code 1006; production wiring asserts the 30s constant.
- **CI note:** unrelated `test-extension` readdirSync flake on compact-small-1.

AI-assisted.

target.title: fix: keep yielded parent runs deferred until subagents settle
target.body:
## Summary

This change promotes yielded-parent semantics into a shared parent lifecycle classifier and routes the affected cron, subagent-registry, and Discord/source-message paths through that state instead of letting each consumer infer completion from terminal-shaped model-attempt events, missing final text, or abort-shaped control flow.

The shipped behavior is:

- yielded parent + active descendants is treated as waiting/deferred, not ordinary completion;
- yielded parent + no descendant is treated as diagnostic error;
- cron delivery waits for a real final outcome instead of counting the yielded attempt as `ok / not-delivered`;
- Discord/source-message progress remains parent-owned while the yielded parent is waiting;
- descendant settlement wakes/reconciles yielded parents through the existing continuation paths.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where parent-agent runs that spawned child sessions/subagents and then called `sessions_yield` could look finished before the parent task actually completed.

The most visible failures were:

- isolated cron `agentTurn` jobs with valid delivery targets could finish as `ok / not-delivered` because the yielded parent had no final payload yet;
- Discord source-message lifecycle could clear parent progress/done indicators while child work was still active or while the parent was waiting to reconcile final output;
- run history/status surfaces made yielded parent work look like delivery failure, ordinary success with no output, or completed source-message work instead of a paused/resumable parent lifecycle.

`session_yield` is supposed to end the current model turn, not the parent task. This PR makes that distinction explicit for the affected runtime consumers.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

Operators and developers can now rely on `sessions_yield` after spawning child/subagent work without the parent run being misrepresented as complete at the cron or Discord lifecycle boundary.

Practically:

- autonomous development crons stop inflating misleading `ok / not-delivered` results for intentionally yielded runs;
- cron history exposes a distinct `deferred` state for yielded parent handoff;
- Discord progress no longer marks the parent source message done just because the parent yielded while children continue;
- yielded parent runs are resumed/reconciled when descendant work settles;
- debugging points to the parent/child lifecycle state instead of falsely implying delivery target resolution failed.

## Linked Context

- #95535 — `sessions_yield` isolated cron resumption/delivery gap.
- #92369 — subagent orchestration in isolated cron sessions needs reliable spawn/wait/aggregate semantics.
- #92116 — `sessions_yield` completion delivered as passive context can break orchestration loops.
- #86537 — subagent terminal reconciliation can expire suspended final delivery.
- #86538 — session write-lock timeouts can block subagent delivery lanes.
- #95833 — subagent abort-settle/session-lock failure can break session continuation.
- #92460 — isolated cron completion delivery gap around final controller return.
- #95604 — Discord subagent progress visibility.
- #94153 — durable queued subagent completion announcements.
- #95847 — requester-consumed descendant completion accounting.

## What Changes

### Shared parent lifecycle state

- Adds `src/agents/agent-lifecycle-parent-state.ts`.
- Classifies lifecycle events with explicit yielded/waiting vs terminal semantics.
- Exports the classifier through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime`.
- Routes subagent registry and Discord source-message handling through the classifier instead of local `yielded && paused` inference.

### Cron lifecycle and delivery

- Adds first-class cron run status `deferred`.
- Classifies yielded descendant handoff before delivery-mode branching, so text, structured payloads, `delivery.mode: none`, source-satisfied delivery, and normal direct delivery all share the same semantics.
- Prevents duplicate/interim parent announcements while descendants are active.
- Records yielded-without-descendant as explicit error diagnostic.
- Keeps deferred manual task runs active rather than failing them.
- Disables one-shot deferred cron jobs after handoff to avoid retry loops.

### Persistence, protocol, CLI, and UI

- Extends run-log JSON/SQLite encoding and status filtering for `deferred`.
- Extends Gateway protocol schemas and cron server filters.
- Extends CLI status/wait typing and docs.
- Extends hook-visible status typing.
- Adds Control UI status/filter labels and generated locale fallbacks.

### Parent/subagent reconciliation

- Tracks yielded/paused parents that still have pending descendants.
- Marks yielded parents with `wakeOnDescendantSettle` so they are resumed/reconciled when descendant work settles.
- Handles child success/failure settlement through existing subagent lifecycle recovery paths.
- Adds regression coverage for yielded parents being reconciled after child failure so diagnostics can wake the parent.

### Discord/source-message lifecycle

- Projects lifecycle events from agent execution into reply/channel handling.
- Uses the shared classifier to identify yielded/waiting parent state.
- Preserves in-progress/progress representation for yielded parents with active children.
- Avoids prematurely marking Discord status reactions done or clearing draft/progress state when the parent yielded and remains waiting.

### Concurrent user-message semantics

`docs/tools/subagents.md` documents the selected policy: if a human sends another message while a requester is yielded, the new message starts a normal turn for the same requester session. OpenClaw keeps the yielded run visible as waiting on descendant completion rather than converting it into a stale final reply; when descendant completion arrives, the completion event is handed back to the requester for synthesis.

## Implementation Notes

Implementation details are included in the What Changes section above; focused evidence and live behavior proof are preserved below.

## Tests / Verification

Focused test coverage plus type, docs, and formatting gates are preserved under Evidence below.

## Evidence

### Rebase/Squash/Proof

- Common upstream base: `13ecca5408cbc94e66105608bfe770d0fc660d76` (`origin/main`, `fix(telegram): back off session init spool retries`)
- Previous PR head: `c163d18fa610687e7dfb8585f1fe8f30b0c4185d`
- Current PR head: `73cff6aa1b0a3ab5786fdfc3a96c98f575e7fcc8`
- Rebased and squashed to one commit on the common base; pushed with `--force-with-lease`.

### ClawSweeper Requested Real Behavior Proof Coverage

ClawSweeper requested redacted live behavior proof for the yielded-parent/deferred lifecycle across the surfaces touched by this PR. This body currently includes the live cron/subagent deferred handoff proof below: a real Dev-01 cron run where the yielded parent remained `deferred` while a descendant was active, with redacted run output, child completion marker, and run/shared-state checks.

Remaining ClawSweeper-requested proof not present in this body yet:

- Redacted Discord visual status/progress/status-reaction proof showing a yielded parent with active descendants remains visibly in progress until descendant settlement.
- Best-effort cron yielded handoff proof/regression after the `deliveryBestEffort` bypass fix, showing best-effort delivery does not incorrectly bypass the yielded-parent deferred lifecycle.
- Migration/upgrade compatibility proof for the detected persistent data-model/status-contract changes.

Maintainer acceptance is still needed for the public `deferred` cron/status/SDK contract; that is a review decision, not something runtime proof alone can certify.

### Real / Live Behavior Proof

Runtime: Dev-01 installed stack commit `5c1fd341c89b1493fed1ea6014388394291450c3` via `/home/kklouzal/update.sh`; `openclaw --version` reported `OpenClaw 2026.6.9 (5c1fd34)` and `openclaw-gateway.service` was active from that stack.

```bash
  --tools sessions_spawn,sessions_yield --timeout-seconds 600 \
  --message 'Live proof marker pr95996-95847-live-20260623T222458Z ...'

openclaw cron run 514fd6e1-862e-43ca-87e3-da1197a7c938 \
  --wait --wait-timeout 12m --poll-interval 5s --timeout 600000
```

Redacted observed output from the live run:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "enqueued": true,
  "runId": "manual:514fd6e1-862e-43ca-87e3-da1197a7c938:1782253518340:1",

    "diagnostics": {

        {

        }

    },

  }
}
```

The non-zero wait exit is expected for this proof: `openclaw cron run --wait` exits non-zero for persisted `deferred` status, while still returning the run record. Follow-up inspection showed the spawned child completed with marker `CHILD_MARKER pr95996-95847-live-20260623T222458Z` and the shared state row recorded `ended_reason = subagent-complete`. The cron shared-state row for the same job persisted `last_run_status = deferred`, `last_delivery_status = not-requested`, and diagnostic summary `cron isolated agent yielded while descendant runs are still active`.

Remaining proof gap: this live proof covers the cron yielded-parent/subagent deferred lifecycle path. It does not provide Discord visual status-reaction proof.

### Focused test coverage

```bash

  src/agents/agent-lifecycle-parent-state.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagent-registry.steer-restart.test.ts \

  extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts \

  ui/src/ui/views/cron.test.ts \
```

target.title: fix(commitments): avoid quadratic heartbeat session discovery
target.body:
Related: #105787

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes heartbeat commitment fan-out latency when many due commitments belong to one session. The existing path loads and expires the JSON store while holding the queue/file lock, releases that lock, then scans the returned in-memory records. For every qualifying due record it rescans the complete store to count recent sent commitments. The quadratic scan is outside the lock, but it delays heartbeat processing and increases heartbeat latency. Reported isolated medians were approximately 191 ms at 1,000, 847 ms at 2,000, and 2.28 s at 4,000 records.

## Why This Change Was Made

The commitments store now builds the rolling 24-hour sent-count map once per agent and reuses it for due-session discovery and single-session due selection. Due-window, snooze, expiry, daily-cap, ordering, limit, agent-scope, queue, and cross-process file-lock behavior remain on the existing path.

This is intentionally an interim JSON-store fix. OpenClaw's shared SQLite state schema already contains a commitments table and indexes, but making it canonical requires a separate JSON-to-SQLite migration/doctor contract and broader persistence coverage. That migration remains a follow-up rather than expanding this focused latency fix.

## User Impact

Heartbeat commitment discovery changes from repeated full-store counting to one aggregation pass plus the existing due-record scan. Large concentrated sessions therefore scale linearly with store size instead of quadratically, without changing which sessions are eligible for delivery.

## Evidence

- Store correctness coverage includes due windows, snoozes, rolling daily caps, agent scope, deterministic session-key ordering, expiry, and concurrent file-store updates.
- The concentrated-session regression uses 8,000 due records in one session and a production-like `limit: 10`, so the base implementation repeatedly rescans the store while the fixed implementation reuses one count map.
- The runner-level regression uses the production heartbeat runner with a real temporary JSON state directory and 16,000 concentrated due records. The model and channel boundaries are stubbed there for deterministic CI coverage.
- Focused validation, using the linked-worktree local fallback:

  ```text
  11 store tests passed; 14 heartbeat-runner tests passed.
  ```

### Real Gateway heartbeat proof

I reran the actual built `dist/index.js gateway` locally in fresh isolated state directories for the baseline and PR. Each run seeded 16,000 pending due commitments plus one recent sent commitment, all concentrated in one Telegram session, then invoked the production Gateway `wake` RPC once. The Gateway scheduler, heartbeat runner, JSON store, due-session selector, Telegram plugin dispatch, and delivery/status updates were real. The model and Telegram Bot API were local HTTP fixtures, so the run was secretless and deterministic; no scheduler, store, runner, or channel-dispatch function was stubbed.

The baseline used main checkout `43901be298`, a descendant of the PR base `6c884691105b`; there were no changes under `src/commitments/` or `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts` between those refs. The PR run used `fcb249f4953485071e123b7cd2fce31f32ea96da`. The redacted terminal output below is one matched run per revision:


target.title: fix: active-memory recall fails with billing rejections on subscription-only Claude CLI setups
target.body:
Closes #106839
Related: #86761

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where agents running on the Claude CLI runtime with subscription-only auth (Claude Code OAuth, no Anthropic API key) would have every active-memory recall either fail with a billing rejection (no extra-usage balance) or **silently draw paid metered extra usage** (extra usage enabled) — while main-session turns correctly ran on plan limits through the CLI backend. Anthropic routing direct anthropic-messages calls on subscription tokens to extra-usage billing is long-standing behavior; the embedded runner's direct-API passthrough (`cli_runtime_passthrough_openclaw`) was never a viable path for these credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an opt-in `RunEmbeddedAgentParams.cliBackendDispatch: "subscription-auth"`: when the run's provider is `claude-cli` — directly or via a canonical `anthropic/<model>` ref whose configured `agentRuntime` is claude-cli — a backend is registered, and the ordered credential selection resolves to subscription (oauth/token) or nothing rather than an API key, the run executes through `runCliAgent` as a one-shot turn. Active-memory recall opts in. The dispatch preserves the embedded run's contracts:

- **Tool restriction is enforced server-side**: `toolsAllow` maps to the selectable-backend surface, bounds the loopback MCP grant (tools outside it can be neither listed nor called, even under bypass permission modes), and restricted runs get an exclusive loopback-only MCP bundle — user/plugin MCP servers are not merged in.
- **Transcript parity**: the run is mirrored into the caller-owned session file (user turn, live tool call/result records, assistant snapshot — flushed immediately on abort), so `persistTranscripts`, timeout partial-text salvage, and the live terminal-search watcher work identically to embedded runs.
- **Isolation**: fresh CLI process per run, no live-session reuse, session-scoped MCP cleanup (never the process-wide loopback server), CLI session bindings dropped from the result.
- **Scope**: claude-cli only; `google-gemini-cli` and custom backends keep the passthrough — their direct-API contracts were not verified and this PR makes no claims about them. An available API key keeps the existing fast passthrough. The core-side provider set could move to a `CliBackendConfig` capability flag if maintainers prefer that seam.

## User Impact

Subscription-only Claude CLI deployments get working active-memory recall on plan limits, consistent with their main turns — instead of failing every turn or silently consuming paid extra usage. Setups with an Anthropic API key see no behavior change. No config changes required; note that CLI-dispatched recalls measured 13.8–16.9s on a dev laptop, so the plugin's default 15s `timeoutMs` is tight — 30s is comfortable.

target.title: fix(polls): add default maximum poll option count
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Matrix polls had no outbound `pollMaxOptions` limit while the Matrix protocol (MSC3381) caps poll options at 20. Other channels (Discord=10, WhatsApp=12, MS Teams=12, Telegram=12) all declare their protocol limits.
- Solution: Declare `pollMaxOptions: 20` in Matrix-owned outbound code and pass `maxOptions: 20` explicitly in `buildPollStartContent`. The shared `normalizePollInput` helper's public contract is unchanged: omitting `maxOptions` means no limit, preserving caller-controlled behavior.
- What changed:
  - `extensions/matrix/src/channel.ts` — added `pollMaxOptions: 20` to `matrixChannelOutbound`
  - `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.ts` — `buildPollStartContent` passes `maxOptions: 20` explicitly to `normalizePollInput`
  - `src/polls.test.ts` — locks in omitted-`maxOptions` = no limit contract
  - `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts` — 20-option boundary tests (accept 20, reject 21)
  - `extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts` — asserts `pollMaxOptions` on static outbound adapter
- What did NOT change: `normalizePollInput` omitted-limit semantics; `src/polls.ts`; other channel implementations; no unrelated UI/avatar changes.

## ClawSweeper review fixes (all P1 findings addressed)

- **P1: Keep the generic poll limit caller-configured** — `src/polls.ts` is untouched. `normalizePollInput` retains its original contract: omitting `maxOptions` means no limit. The 20-option Matrix protocol limit lives entirely in Matrix-owned code: `matrixChannelOutbound.pollMaxOptions = 20` and `buildPollStartContent(..., { maxOptions: 20 })`. A regression test locks in the omitted-limit = no limit behavior.
- **P1: Drop the unrelated avatar commit** — The branch has been force-pushed from a clean `origin/main` base. All unrelated Control UI avatar changes from #104912 are removed.
- **P1: Rebase to clean mergeable head** — The branch is now a single commit on top of latest `origin/main`, no conflicts.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Matrix polls were missing the 20-option protocol limit. Now enforced at the Matrix boundary.
- **Real environment tested:** Vitest unit tests for Matrix poll types, Matrix outbound adapter, and shared poll helper contract.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  pnpm test src/polls.test.ts
  pnpm test extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  # src/polls.test.ts — 7 passed
  - "does not limit options when maxOptions is omitted" → 50 options accepted ✓

  # extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts — 11 passed
  - "accepts exactly 20 poll options per MSC3381" → answers.length = 20 ✓
  - "rejects more than 20 poll options per MSC3381" → throws "at most 20" ✓

  # extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts — 6 passed
  - "declares a 20-option poll maximum..." → outbound.pollMaxOptions = 20 ✓
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Matrix 20-option protocol limit enforced at Matrix boundary. Public helper contract preserved (omitted `maxOptions` = no limit).

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test files: `src/polls.test.ts`, `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts`, `extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Matrix: 20 options accepted, 21 rejected (protocol boundary in `buildPollStartContent`)
  - Matrix outbound: `pollMaxOptions = 20` declared on static adapter
  - Public helper: omitted `maxOptions` does not limit (contract preserved)

## Root Cause

- Root cause: Matrix outbound adapter did not declare `pollMaxOptions`, unlike all other poll channel adapters (Discord, WhatsApp, MS Teams, Telegram).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No Matrix-owned poll option limit enforcement.

target.title: fix(qa-channel): add timeout to qa-bus state guarded fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `getQaBusState` called `fetchWithSsrFGuard` with no `timeoutMs` and no `AbortSignal`, so a loopback qa-bus peer that accepted TCP but never returned headers could hang Gateway/QA tooling forever (body idle caps never start).

## Why This Change Was Made

- Pass `timeoutMs: QA_BUS_STATE_TIMEOUT_MS` (10s) through the existing guarded fetch, matching Feishu registration / similar Type C hang floors.
- Optional `options.timeoutMs` overrides for hermetic hang regressions only; production callers omit it.
- No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A hung qa-bus `/v1/state` peer could pin state inspection indefinitely.

**After:** State fetches fail closed after 10s with `TimeoutError` so QA/monitor loops can continue.

## Evidence

Head: `cadb067c5abd997f396198b41094afd7e150eff2`

### Executable negative control + fix proof

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-channel/src/bus-client.test.ts -- --run -t "negative control|never returns headers" --reporter=verbose
```

```text
[qa-channel bus-state negative control] outcome=still-pending wait_ms=200 without_timeoutMs=true
[qa-channel bus-state hang proof] timed_out=true name=TimeoutError elapsed_ms=85 production_timeout_ms=10000
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed | 6 skipped (8)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** `/v1/state` guarded fetch hangs forever when peer accepts TCP but never returns headers.
- **Canonical path:** `getQaBusState` → production `fetchWithSsrFGuard` with `timeoutMs: QA_BUS_STATE_TIMEOUT_MS` (10s) / test override.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime HTTP; real loopback `node:http` never-headers peer; production SSRF-guarded transport (negative control calls `fetchWithSsrFGuard` with **no** `timeoutMs`).
- **After fix:** `TimeoutError` in ~80ms with override; production floor is the exported 10s constant.
- **CI note:** `checks-node-compact-small-1` `readdirSync: 54` flake is unrelated tooling.

target.title: fix: Control UI avatar initial breaks on emoji display names
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: When an agent's display name begins with an emoji or other astral Unicode character, the Control UI sidebar and agent selector rendered a broken or garbled avatar initial (a lone UTF-16 surrogate half / replacement character) instead of the intended glyph.
- Solution: Replaced `(label || agent.id).slice(0, 1).toUpperCase()` with a new `deriveAvatarInitial` helper that uses `Intl.Segmenter` with `granularity: "grapheme"` to extract the complete first user-perceived character (grapheme cluster). When `Intl.Segmenter` is unavailable (Firefox 114-124), falls back to the first complete Unicode code point (surrogate pair-aware). Returns `""` for empty or missing input.
- What changed: `ui/src/lib/avatar.ts` — `deriveAvatarInitial` using `Intl.Segmenter` with feature detection and fallback; `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` — uses helper; `ui/src/components/agent-select.ts` — uses helper in fallback.
- What did NOT change: Behavior for ordinary ASCII names; other `.slice()` sites left unchanged (ASCII-only inputs).

## ClawSweeper review fixes

**P1: Guard Intl.Segmenter before rendering avatars** — Added feature detection: checks `typeof Intl.Segmenter === "function"` at runtime. When unavailable (e.g., Firefox 114-124), falls back to extracting the first complete Unicode code point (surrogate pair-aware). This prevents runtime errors in browsers without `Intl.Segmenter` support while still improving behavior over the original UTF-16 code unit slicing.

**P2: Preserve complete first grapheme** — Previously used `codePointAt(0)` which only gets the first code point, still truncating joined emoji (👨‍👩‍👧‍👦→👨), flags (🇺🇸→🇺), skin-tone sequences (👍🏻→👍). Now uses `Intl.Segmenter` with `granularity: "grapheme"` to extract the complete first grapheme cluster.

**P2: Reuse fallback in agent selector** — `AgentSelect.renderAvatar` previously used `normalizeAgentLabel(agent)[0]` (first UTF-16 code unit). Now uses `deriveAvatarInitial(normalizeAgentLabel(agent))` for consistency with the sidebar.

## Browser Compatibility

- **With Intl.Segmenter** (Firefox 125+, Chrome 87+, Safari 14.1+): Complete grapheme clusters preserved for joined emoji, flags, skin-tone sequences
- **Without Intl.Segmenter** (Firefox 114-124): First complete code point extracted (surrogate pair-aware), preventing dangling surrogates for astral emoji like 😀 or 🚀

## Real behavior proof

### Testing Approach

This PR uses **jsdom with real Lit component rendering** rather than Playwright for the following reasons:

1. **Real component execution**: The tests import and render the actual `AgentSelect` Lit component, not a mock or stub. The component's render method executes the same code path as production.

2. **Real DOM manipulation**: Lit creates real DOM elements with the computed text content. The test asserts against `element.textContent`, which is the same value users see in the browser.

3. **Grapheme cluster verification**: The tests verify the exact grapheme boundaries:
   - `👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family` → `👨‍👩‍👧‍👦` (complete family emoji, not just `👨`)
   - `🇺🇸Flag` → `🇺🇸` (complete flag, not just `🇺`)
   - `👍🏻Thumbs` → `👍🏻` (emoji with skin tone modifier)

4. **Browser compatibility**: The unavailable-API test verifies the Firefox 114-124 fallback path doesn't throw and produces correct surrogate-pair-aware results.

### Why jsdom is sufficient

- **Same code path**: Both jsdom and browsers execute the same JavaScript code for grapheme segmentation.
- **Same output**: The `Intl.Segmenter` API behaves identically in jsdom and browsers when available.
- **Fallback tested**: The feature-detection + fallback path is explicitly tested.
- **Precedent**: The sibling plugin-monogram PR uses the same jsdom approach for grapheme testing.

### Test evidence

```bash
pnpm test ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts
pnpm test ui/src/components/agent-select.test.ts
```

```text
✓ deriveAvatarInitial with Intl.Segmenter: preserves complete grapheme clusters
  - "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family" → "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦"
  - "🇺🇸Flag" → "🇺🇸"
  - "👍🏻Thumbs" → "👍🏻"

✓ deriveAvatarInitial without Intl.Segmenter (Firefox 114-124): surrogate pair fallback
  - "😀Name" → "😀" (surrogate pair preserved)
  - "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family" → "👨" (first code point, no error)

✓ AgentSelect DOM render with grapheme-leading name:
  - Real Lit component renders with textContent = "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦"
```

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test + Component test
- Target test files: `ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts`, `ui/src/components/agent-select.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Helper: emoji initial, joined emoji grapheme, flag grapheme, skin-tone grapheme, ASCII, empty/null
  - Helper fallback: unavailable Intl.Segmenter path with surrogate pair preservation
  - Selector: grapheme cluster preserved in real Lit component DOM render
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Asserts the exact grapheme boundary at both helper and component level, plus browser compatibility path.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: Avatar initial used `.slice(0, 1)` (first UTF-16 code unit) and later `codePointAt(0)` (first code point), neither of which respects grapheme cluster boundaries.
- Missing detection / guardrail: No grapheme-aware initial derivation; agent selector had a separate inconsistent fallback; no Intl.Segmenter feature detection for browser compatibility.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where subagent SQLite loading could import the legacy JSON registry, commit the rows, and then fail while unlinking the JSON source. If canonical rows were later emptied, the stale JSON could be imported again and resurrect old runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Legacy import now runs only from automatic doctor/state migration. The runtime loader reads SQLite only. Imported rows and a durable `migration_sources`/`migration_runs` receipt commit in one synchronous SQLite transaction; cleanup atomically claims the exact source before deletion and remains retryable on `EPERM`, process interruption, or receipt-finalization failure. Stable source identity, exact-byte parsing, content guards, and partial receipts prevent changed, malformed, or ambiguous legacy files from being reinterpreted as new canonical state.

## User Impact

After migration, runtime reads cannot fall back to `runs.json`. A failed legacy-file cleanup produces a doctor warning, but retrying doctor does not re-import or resurrect runs after canonical SQLite state changes. Valid records from a partially malformed source are imported once while the source remains available for recovery; ambiguous pre-receipt sources are preserved and reported instead of being silently guessed.

## Evidence

- Formal current-main fault injection: an injected `EPERM` after SQLite import produced `firstLoadError=EPERM`, left one SQLite row and the JSON source, and a later empty canonical load returned `resurrected=["stale-run"]`.
- After-fix real doctor-owned migration proof (redacted terminal log; temporary state only):

- Added deterministic coverage in `src/agents/subagent-registry.store.sqlite.test.ts` for v1 import, partial import, `EPERM` cleanup retry, changed/unreadable source handling, and post-commit crash recovery.
- Updated large-2 persistence/resume and large-3 gateway session-utils fixtures to seed canonical SQLite state; the old test-only JSON read-through flag is gone. Small-7 state-migration coverage now asserts against the explicit migration environment.
- Added automatic doctor/state-migration wiring coverage in `src/infra/state-migrations.test.ts`.
- Static validation passed: `oxfmt --check`, focused Oxlint, and `git diff --check`; an earlier full-branch repository autoreview of the production migration fix completed with no accepted/actionable findings. The final commit adds only SQLite-canonical test seams and was validated by the focused proof below.

The temporary real-proof test also passed in both agents projects; the repository’s approved remote Testbox was unavailable.

- PR CI initially caught three affected-surface issues during iteration: missing state-migration result aggregation, an explicit-env test assertion, and JSON-only persistence/session-utils fixtures; all are fixed in the current pushed head. Large-2, large-3, and small-7 failure logs were inspected before this update.

target.title: fix(reef): bound relay HTTP JSON response body reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Reef users could have the relay HTTP client buffer an unbounded JSON response body when a misbehaving or hostile relay returned oversized success or error payloads on `ReefTransportClient` request paths (auth, friends, mail pull/send/ack).

Related sibling surface: open #106439 bounds Reef *guard* provider responses in `extensions/reef/protocol/guard-adapters.ts`; this PR covers the separate relay transport client in `extensions/reef/src/transport.ts`, which still used unbounded `response.json()`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ReefTransportClient.request` now reads JSON through the shared `readProviderJsonResponse` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-http`:

- success bodies capped at 16 MiB (`reef.relay`)
- error bodies capped at 64 KiB (`reef.relay.error`), with the existing status-code fallback preserved when the error body is missing, malformed, or oversized

Oversized streams are cancelled before the remainder is buffered. Non-goal: changing guard adapters (owned by #106439) or adding new config.

## User Impact

Reef relay HTTP calls fail closed on oversized JSON instead of allocating unbounded memory. Normal-sized relay responses and bounded error messages continue to work as before.

## Evidence

Head: `7d4ab0a3461a71021bd0d0ba53d5aade8573206f`

**Head:** `f8d35557ae69c3e457b601cbe2bc535049689032`

**Behavior addressed:** Hostile/oversized relay JSON no longer forces unbounded `response.json()` allocation; streams cancel after the byte budget.

**Real environment tested:** Linux WSL2, Node `v22.22.0`, local checkout of this branch.

### Path-level proof (production `ReefTransportClient` + negative control)

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-reef-relay-json-bound.ts
success overflow cancelled=true emittedBytes=16908288 error=reef.relay: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes
error overflow name=ReefRelayError status=503 message=relay HTTP 503 cancelled=true emittedBytes=81920
negative control response.json() cancelled=false emittedBytes=262144
ok
```

Interpretation:

- success path offered ~20 MiB, cancelled after `16908288` bytes (~16 MiB + one 64 KiB chunk)
- error path offered 128 KiB against a 64 KiB cap, cancelled after `81920` bytes, still threw `ReefRelayError` with `relay HTTP 503`
- negative control: the same tracked-stream shape drained fully under unbounded `response.json()` with `cancelled=false`

target.title: fix(agents): bound compaction planning worker payloads
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the compaction planning and worker handoff paths, checked duplicate/open PR state for #100635, and independently reviewed and validated the branch locally.

## What Problem This Solves

Addresses #100635.

Compaction planning sanitizes private fields before worker handoff, but previously still sent full model-visible tool-result text and base64 image data through `workerData`. Large browser/command results or multimodal transcripts could therefore force multi-megabyte structured-clone work before summary-prompt truncation had a chance to help.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a planning-only projection before worker handoff:

- oversized tool-result text/content keeps a bounded UTF-16-safe sample plus omitted-character accounting;
- image blocks in user, custom, and tool-result content keep type/MIME metadata but omit base64 bytes;
- token-pressure accounting remains conservative, so chunking and pruning decisions still reflect the original payload;
- local fallback behavior and private-field sanitization remain unchanged.

Image bytes are not used by compaction's text serializer, while image token pressure is a fixed per-block estimate. Omitting only `data` therefore reduces worker cloning without changing summary text or planning pressure. The projection helper is split from worker orchestration so both implementation files stay within the repository LOC guard.

## User Impact

Long or multimodal sessions should spend less time and memory cloning redundant payloads into the compaction planning worker, reducing event-loop stall and OOM risk without changing compaction decisions or generated summary text.

## Evidence

Final rebase:

- `upstream/main`: `055f6649f97`
- branch head: `4716b38781e`

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where WhatsApp inbound media downloads that stall after Baileys returns a stream (headers/start ok, then no further chunks) would block `downloadInboundMedia` forever via `saveMediaStream`'s unbounded `for await`, so inbound dispatch never produces an agent reply for that message.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Wrap the Baileys AsyncIterable with a local per-chunk idle race (production default `30_000` ms), matching Telegram's download idle floor and the LINE channel pattern (open `#86873`, different owner).
- On timeout, reject with `WhatsAppInboundMediaTimeoutError`, call `iterator.return()` so Node Readable streams are destroyed, and silence the losing `next()` to avoid `unhandledRejection`.
- Tests may pass a short `chunkTimeoutMs`; production omits it and uses the 30s floor (proven with fake timers).
- Does **not** change core `saveMediaStream` / `src/media/store.ts` (avoids competing with LINE `#86873`).
- Timeout error class stays module-private (knip unused-export gate).

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled WhatsApp media body could hang inbound handling for that message indefinitely.

**After:** Idle streams fail closed after 30s with a clear timeout error so the monitor loop can continue.

## Summary
- Problem: Four locations decode base64 payloads before checking size limits, risking transient OOM if a provider/tool returns an oversized payload.
- Solution: Add estimate-before-decode guards where safe, preserve existing behavior contracts where compatibility matters.
- What changed:
  - `src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.ts`: writeCliImages adds maxBytes param, estimates decoded size before Buffer.from
  - `src/image-generation/image-assets.ts`: Estimates decoded size before canonicalization to avoid transient string allocation; propagates maxBytes through `generatedImageAssetFromBase64`, `generatedImageAssetFromOpenAiCompatibleEntry`, and `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse`
  - `src/image-generation/openai-compatible-image-provider.ts`: Wires `resolveGeneratedMediaMaxBytes(req.cfg, "image")` into `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse`
  - `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts`: Wires `resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes` into OpenAI image generation path
  - `extensions/google/image-generation-provider.ts`: Wires `resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes` into Google image generation path
  - `extensions/openrouter/image-generation-provider.ts`: Wires `resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes` into OpenRouter image extraction path
- What did NOT change: `resizeImage` still attempts resize before rejecting (maxBytes is an output target, not an input ceiling); `generatedMusicAssetFromBase64` still returns guaranteed result for SDK compatibility.

## Real behavior proof
- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Base64 decode-before-bounds defense-in-depth gap with attention to compatibility.
- **Real environment tested:** Task worktree on final head `bfbad1ed57` (rebased on latest `upstream/main`), with `node --import tsx` direct function invocation exercising the actual provider response parser and CLI image-write path.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

  The script calls `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse` with `maxBytes` from `resolveGeneratedMediaMaxBytes` (the same wiring used by the OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter, and generic compatible provider paths), and `writeCliImages` with `maxBytes` from `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`.

- **Evidence after fix (final head bfbad1ed57):**
  ```text

  --- Part 1: Provider response path (parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse) ---

  Configured maxBytes for image: 6291456 bytes (6.0 MB)
  Default MAX_IMAGE_BYTES: 6291456 bytes (6.0 MB)

    image[0].fileName: image-1.png

    estimated decoded bytes: 6292480

  === Proof complete ===
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:**
  1. Provider path: valid configured-size payload (100 bytes) accepted and parsed into image asset; oversized payload (6292480 bytes > 6291456 budget) rejected before decode with 0 images returned
  2. CLI image-write path: valid image (50 bytes) written to disk successfully; oversized image (6292480 bytes > 6291456 budget) rejected with error before Buffer.from allocation

target.title: fix(agents): decouple MCP retirement from browser cleanup
target.body:
Related: #76233
Related: #101830

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a completed run-mode subagent waits for sequential browser-tab cleanup before retiring its bundle MCP runtime and starting completion delivery. A browser close request can wait up to the browser service timeout per tab, so one run with several tabs can delay MCP retirement, the completion announcement, and the next same-session turn.

The concrete sequential browser-cleanup delay is separate from the MCP lease-disposal race covered by #76233 and the related #101830 work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browser cleanup is dispatched as independent owner-scoped work, while MCP retirement and completion announcement proceed after the existing generation and lease-safety checks. Browser operations hold a per-session access gate for their full request; cleanup takes the exclusive gate, so a successor browser turn waits safely instead of racing an already-issued close request.

The browser registry tracks the opaque run owner and an ordered ownership claim. Successor reuse transfers ownership; late predecessor callbacks cannot reclaim or remove the successor tab. Failed non-ignorable closes remain tracked for a later cleanup, and legacy unowned tabs remain eligible for cleanup.

`runId` remains an additive, optional Plugin SDK context field. It is host-issued, stable for the active run, opaque, and absent outside an active run. Plugins may use it only to key ephemeral plugin-owned resources and cleanup; they must not parse it, persist it as application data, expose it to users, or use it as an authentication or authorization boundary. The contract is documented in `docs/plugins/building-plugins.md` and covered at the `defineToolPlugin` factory boundary in `src/plugin-sdk/tool-plugin.test.ts`; the existing agent-context test covers runtime propagation.

## User Impact

Run-mode subagent completion no longer waits for the browser service to close every tracked tab before MCP retirement and completion delivery begin. A successor turn can start its non-browser work immediately and its browser work is admitted after the old cleanup gate releases, preserving tab safety. App-view MCP leases continue to defer retirement until their release path completes.

## Evidence

Branch-attributable CI repair:

- `check-test-types` previously failed at `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts(345,18)` because the successor fixture read optional `entry.startedAt`. - `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts`: 88/88 passed.
- `src/plugin-sdk/tool-plugin.test.ts`: 6/6 passed.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.plugin-context.test.ts`: 20/20 passed.

target.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits at 30s
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using Codex app-server over `websocket`/`unix` transport would hang forever on `initialize`/RPC when a peer accepted TCP but never completed the WebSocket upgrade. Pending frames never flush and the client never sees a transport exit, so the run cannot fail closed or reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add a private `buildCodexAppServerWebSocketOptions` that sets `handshakeTimeout: 30_000` (same floor as Slack relay / Mattermost / Discord gateway).
- Both TCP and Unix upgrade paths consume that builder.
- Guard `EventEmitter` error re-emit with `listenerCount` so callers that only wait on `exit` (handshake hang paths) are not disrupted by Node's unhandled-`error` throw.
- Regressions observe production wiring in source (knip-safe) and prove stalled-handshake exit + `initialize` failure with a short test-only hang floor.

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A Codex app-server endpoint that accepted TCP without completing the websocket handshake could pin `initialize`/RPC forever on that attempt.

**After:** Handshake waits fail closed after 30s (`Opening handshake has timed out` → transport `exit` / client error), so the run can stop or recover instead of hanging.

## Evidence

Head: `a02be68e1107857c4808cc9e93e1af5b10c7f1f1`

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```text
[codex handshake proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=200 code=1006 handshakeTimeout_ms=200 production_ms=30000
```

target.title: fix: Control UI avatar initial breaks on emoji display names
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: When an agent's display name begins with an emoji or other astral Unicode character, the Control UI sidebar and agent selector rendered a broken or garbled avatar initial (a lone UTF-16 surrogate half / replacement character) instead of the intended glyph.
- Solution: Replaced `(label || agent.id).slice(0, 1).toUpperCase()` with a new `deriveAvatarInitial` helper that uses `Intl.Segmenter` with `granularity: "grapheme"` to extract the complete first user-perceived character (grapheme cluster). When `Intl.Segmenter` is unavailable (Firefox 114-124), falls back to the first complete Unicode code point (surrogate pair-aware). Returns `""` for empty or missing input.
- What changed: `ui/src/lib/avatar.ts` — `deriveAvatarInitial` using `Intl.Segmenter` with feature detection and fallback; `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` — uses helper; `ui/src/components/agent-select.ts` — uses helper in fallback.
- What did NOT change: Behavior for ordinary ASCII names; other `.slice()` sites left unchanged (ASCII-only inputs).

## ClawSweeper review fixes

**P1: Guard Intl.Segmenter before rendering avatars** — Added feature detection: checks `typeof Intl.Segmenter === "function"` at runtime. When unavailable (e.g., Firefox 114-124), falls back to extracting the first complete Unicode code point (surrogate pair-aware). This prevents runtime errors in browsers without `Intl.Segmenter` support while still improving behavior over the original UTF-16 code unit slicing.

**P2: Preserve complete first grapheme** — Previously used `codePointAt(0)` which only gets the first code point, still truncating joined emoji (👨‍👩‍👧‍👦→👨), flags (🇺🇸→🇺), skin-tone sequences (👍🏻→👍). Now uses `Intl.Segmenter` with `granularity: "grapheme"` to extract the complete first grapheme cluster.

**P2: Reuse fallback in agent selector** — `AgentSelect.renderAvatar` previously used `normalizeAgentLabel(agent)[0]` (first UTF-16 code unit). Now uses `deriveAvatarInitial(normalizeAgentLabel(agent))` for consistency with the sidebar.

## Browser Compatibility

- **With Intl.Segmenter** (Firefox 125+, Chrome 87+, Safari 14.1+): Complete grapheme clusters preserved for joined emoji, flags, skin-tone sequences
- **Without Intl.Segmenter** (Firefox 114-124): First complete code point extracted (surrogate pair-aware), preventing dangling surrogates for astral emoji like 😀 or 🚀

## Real behavior proof

### Testing Approach

This PR uses **jsdom with real Lit component rendering** rather than Playwright for the following reasons:

1. **Real component execution**: The tests import and render the actual `AgentSelect` Lit component, not a mock or stub. The component's render method executes the same code path as production.

2. **Real DOM manipulation**: Lit creates real DOM elements with the computed text content. The test asserts against `element.textContent`, which is the same value users see in the browser.

3. **Grapheme cluster verification**: The tests verify the exact grapheme boundaries:
   - `👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family` → `👨‍👩‍👧‍👦` (complete family emoji, not just `👨`)
   - `🇺🇸Flag` → `🇺🇸` (complete flag, not just `🇺`)
   - `👍🏻Thumbs` → `👍🏻` (emoji with skin tone modifier)

4. **Browser compatibility**: The unavailable-API test verifies the Firefox 114-124 fallback path doesn't throw and produces correct surrogate-pair-aware results.

### Why jsdom is sufficient

- **Same code path**: Both jsdom and browsers execute the same JavaScript code for grapheme segmentation.
- **Same output**: The `Intl.Segmenter` API behaves identically in jsdom and browsers when available.
- **Fallback tested**: The feature-detection + fallback path is explicitly tested.
- **Precedent**: The sibling plugin-monogram PR uses the same jsdom approach for grapheme testing.

### Test evidence

```bash
pnpm test ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts
pnpm test ui/src/components/agent-select.test.ts
```

```text
✓ deriveAvatarInitial with Intl.Segmenter: preserves complete grapheme clusters
  - "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family" → "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦"
  - "🇺🇸Flag" → "🇺🇸"
  - "👍🏻Thumbs" → "👍🏻"

✓ deriveAvatarInitial without Intl.Segmenter (Firefox 114-124): surrogate pair fallback
  - "😀Name" → "😀" (surrogate pair preserved)
  - "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family" → "👨" (first code point, no error)

✓ AgentSelect DOM render with grapheme-leading name:
  - Real Lit component renders with textContent = "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦"
```

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test + Component test
- Target test files: `ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts`, `ui/src/components/agent-select.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Helper: emoji initial, joined emoji grapheme, flag grapheme, skin-tone grapheme, ASCII, empty/null
  - Helper fallback: unavailable Intl.Segmenter path with surrogate pair preservation
  - Selector: grapheme cluster preserved in real Lit component DOM render
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Asserts the exact grapheme boundary at both helper and component level, plus browser compatibility path.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: Avatar initial used `.slice(0, 1)` (first UTF-16 code unit) and later `codePointAt(0)` (first code point), neither of which respects grapheme cluster boundaries.
- Missing detection / guardrail: No grapheme-aware initial derivation; agent selector had a separate inconsistent fallback; no Intl.Segmenter feature detection for browser compatibility.

target.title: fix(zalo): bound proxy fetcher cache to 64 entries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Zalo `resolveZaloProxyFetch` retained one `makeProxyFetch` entry per distinct proxy URL in a process-lifetime `Map` with no eviction. Config churn or high-cardinality proxy URLs could therefore grow gateway memory without a hard bound.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Cap `proxyCache` at 64 entries using the shared `pruneMapToMaxSize` helper after every successful insert (same pattern as Nextcloud Talk room cache / MS Teams team-group cache / Mattermost opaque-target cache).
- Insertion-order eviction keeps newest proxy fetchers; cache-hit identity and empty-URL behavior are unchanged.
- Adds a focused regression that fills `max+1` distinct URLs, proves the oldest entry is rebuilt on next use, and confirms a mid-window entry still hits.

No new config/env surface. Does not change Bot API timeouts (`#104017`) or other Zalo send paths.

## User Impact

**Before:** Long-running Zalo gateways could retain an unbounded number of proxy fetcher closures as distinct proxy URLs appeared.

**After:** At most 64 distinct proxy fetchers are retained; older ones are dropped and rebuilt on next use.

## Evidence
